newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Opposition alleges Sri Lanka poll was rigged.
newsitem.headline: Opposition alleges Sri Lanka poll was rigged.

text.p: Sri Lanka's main opposition United National Party (UNP) on Sunday accused the government of intimidating voters and rigging local government elections.
"If not for the intimidation and rigging, the result would have been a photo finish," former prime minister and UNP leader Ranil Wickremesinghe told a news conference.

"They (government supporters) just walked in with weapons and stuffed ballot boxes," he said. President Chandrika Kumaratunga's ruling People's Alliance (PA) coalition swept to a landslide victory in last Friday's poll, widely seen as a mid-term appraisal of its performance since it won power in 1994 and ended 17 years of UNP rule.
Elections Commissioner Dayananda Dissanayake said the PA won 194 councils and the UNP 43 of the 238 local bodies at stake. One council was won by an independent group.
Dissanayake said on state television the PA got 49 percent of the total votes polled against the UNP's 41.25 percent. The rest were split between smaller parties and independent groups.
Wickremesinghe said voters had rejected the government's appeal to approve its performance as it polled only 49 percent of the votes against 62 percent at the 1994 presidential poll.
"This is the beginning of the end of the government and a comeback for the UNP," he said. "We can defeat the government at the next general election. We have come within striking distance of it."
Wickremesinghe said the unusually high percentage polled -- up to 77 percent -- indicated the extent of the rigging.
"This is the first local government poll in which voters polled far more than parliamentary or general elections," he said. "This never happened before."
Elections Commissioner Dayananda Dissanayake has said the poll was fair.
He said 77 percent of some 10 million eligible voters had cast ballots in the election, up from 61 percent in the previous 1991 local polls.
